method: The conversion treats a pace on a gradient as work done against the energy cost of running at that gradient, and asks what flat pace would cost the same. Cost of transport follows Minetti's running polynomial, 155.4i^5 - 30.4i^4 - 43.3i^3 + 46.3i^2 + 19.5i + 3.6 joules per kilogram per metre, with i the gradient as a fraction and 3.6 the flat cost, so a pace on a grade multiplied by 3.6 divided by the grade cost is the flat-equivalent pace and the reverse direction multiplies by the grade cost and divides by 3.6. The two directions are exact inverses because one divides by the same ratio the other multiplies by. Grade is entered as a percentage and limited to plus or minus 25 percent, inside the published curve's useful range but well short of its 45 percent limit, and zero grade returns the pace unchanged. Paces must be minutes:seconds with two-digit seconds from 00 to 59, between 2:00 and 30:00 per kilometre or 3:15 and 48:00 per mile; an equivalent outside 1:30 to 60:00 per unit is rejected rather than shown, and exponent notation, blanks and extra decimals are refused instead of parsed. Reported speed is the adjusted pace converted to km/h and mph, and vertical gain is the gradient applied to a kilometre or a mile. The model assumes steady running on a uniform gradient and ignores wind, surface, altitude, heat, technique, fatigue and the difference between treadmill belt speed and overground running; it gives a training reference, not a prediction, race plan or medical advice. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Minetti AE, Moia C, Roi GS, Susta D, Ferretti G, Energy cost of walking and running at extreme uphill and downhill slopes, Journal of Applied Physiology 93:1039-1046 (2002): the fifth-order polynomial used here.
Margaria R, Cerretelli P, Aghemo P, Sassi G, Energy cost of running, Journal of Applied Physiology 18:367-370 (1963): flat running costs about 3.6 J per kg per metre.
American College of Sports Medicine, Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription: gradient raises the metabolic cost of running and treadmill grade is a standard way to set that load.
Grade-adjusted pace as used in endurance training: pace is normalised by the relative energy cost of the gradient so efforts on different terrain can be compared.
